newsitem.title: USA: Maine court says scholarship cut not true punishment.
newsitem.headline: Maine court says scholarship cut not true punishment.

text.p: The Maine Supreme Court Thursday rejected a university student's claim that he could not be prosecuted for assault because the incident had already cost him part of an athletic scholarship.

Roan Sterling argued that because the University of Maine had already punished him, any attempt to prosecute him on criminal charges violated his constitutional protection against being punished twice for the same offence.

Sterling, a football player, was accused of assaulting a teammate in March 1995. A school disciplinary board suspended Sterling, and his coach revoked $2,500 from the annual scholarship that was to pay for room and board.
The coach told school officials at the time it was his policy to revoke the room and board portion of scholarships from athletes who violated the school's disciplinary code.
The justices ruled unanimously that receiving a scholarship was a privilege, not an absolute right, and that any revocation was designed to protect the university's integrity, not to punish Sterling.
